# Environment maps

Day and night are photographic HDRIs from [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com), CC0 (public domain):

| scene | source | files |
|-------|--------|-------|
| day | [Driving School](https://polyhaven.com/a/driving_school) (Dimitrios Savva, Jarod Guest) | `day.hdr`, `day_bg.jpg` |
| night | [Hansaplatz](https://polyhaven.com/a/hansaplatz) (Sergej Majboroda) | `night.hdr`, `night_bg.jpg` |

The studio is generated: `tools/tex/studio_env.py` writes `studio.hdr`, a car-photography studio
(one large overhead softbox, two strip boxes, dark ceiling, white cyc wall band, and a floor that
reads dark close to the car) that gives brushed steel the light-over-dark flank gradient of the
studio reference photos (`ref/studio`). The camera sees a separate white cyclorama set
(`makeCyc` in `web/js/env.js`).

`tools/tex/prep_hdri.py` turns the 4k day/night downloads into what the viewer loads:

- The over-bright key light (sun, lamp or softbox core) is clamped out of the map. Its energy and
  mean direction are measured and stored in `env.json` (`keyDir`, `keyIrradiance`), and
  `web/js/env.js` puts a shadow-casting `DirectionalLight` there, so the car's shadow comes from
  the same place as the light in the photo.
- `*.hdr`: 2048 x 1024 Radiance (RLE) of the clamped map, for PMREM lighting and reflections.
- `*_bg.jpg`: 4096 x 2048 sRGB backdrop holding `srgb(L * backdropScale)`. The viewer projects
  it onto a `GroundedSkybox` (camera height 1.65 m) and divides by `backdropScale` in the
  material colour, so it renders at the HDR's real radiance under the same exposure.

Direction convention: three.js equirect lookup (`u = atan2(z, x) / 2π + 0.5`, top row = +Y);
car front = +X. A preset with `keyAzimuth` turns its map (`environmentRotation` /
`backgroundRotation`) so the key light sits where the preset wants it; the generated studio is
already laid out around the car.

Re-create (after downloading the HDRIs into `<src>`):

```bash
python3 tools/tex/prep_hdri.py <src> web/assets/env day=driving_school_4k.hdr:40:0.32 night=hansaplatz_4k.hdr:25:1.6
python3 tools/tex/studio_env.py
```

# Textures (`../tex/`)

All maps tile seamlessly and are generated by `tools/tex/gen_textures.py`, using FFT-shaped
periodic noise and periodic Voronoi. Normal maps are tangent space, OpenGL convention
(+Y = green = up), so set `normalMap.colorSpace = NoColorSpace` (the default). Roughness and
greyscale maps are linear.

| file | size | use |
|------|------|-----|
| `brushed_n.png` | 2048² | Brushed stainless: fine streaks running along **U**, a few deeper scratches, very faint low-frequency waviness. Use with `anisotropy` (direction = U/tangent). Suggested scale: one tile ≈ 0.5–1.0 m. `normalScale` 0.3–1.0. |
| `brushed_r.png` | 2048² | Roughness variation centred at 0.5, with streaks along U. Use it as `roughnessMap` with `roughness` ≈ 0.45–0.6 so it averages to ~0.25–0.3. |
| `leather_n.png` | 1024² | Pebble-grain leather (~5200 cells per tile). One tile ≈ 0.15 m gives ~2 mm pebbles. `normalScale` ≈ 0.6–1. |
| `leather_r.png` | 1024² | Leather roughness variation (≈0.55, rougher in the grain valleys). |
| `carpet_c.png` | 1024² | Neutral grey loop-pile albedo detail (sRGB). Multiply by the carpet colour. One tile ≈ 0.25 m. |
| `carpet_n.png` | 1024² | Matching loop-pile normal. |
| `plastic_grain_n.png` | 1024² | Fine stipple for dashboard and console plastics. One tile ≈ 0.1–0.2 m, `normalScale` ≈ 0.3–0.6. |
| `tyre_tread_n.png` | 1024 x 256 | Tread micro-detail: slanted sipes repeating 64x around U plus rubber grain. U runs around the circumference. |
| `glass_dirt.png` | 1024² | Subtle smudge and dust mask, 0 = clean. Use it to add to glass roughness or reduce clearcoat. |
